q: What is the most sampled song of all time?
a: "Amen, Brother" by The Winstons (1969). WhoSampled, a user-contributed database, listed 6,873 uses as of July 2025, and Guinness World Records holds it as the most sampled track.

q: Did the Amen break drummer ever get paid?
a: No. Gregory "G.C." Coleman died in 2006 without royalties for the break. A 2015 GoFundMe for bandleader and copyright owner Richard Spencer shows £24,000 raised; the BBC reported more than £18,000 handed over.

q: Where does the famous shout in "Think" come from?
a: Lyn Collins's "Think (About It)" (1972), written and produced by James Brown with Jabo Starks on drums. Its best-known use is Rob Base and DJ E-Z Rock's "It Takes Two" (1988).

q: Who played the "Funky Drummer" break, and did he get royalties?
a: Clyde Stubblefield, on a James Brown single released in 1970. He was not listed as a songwriter and received little or no royalties; he died in 2017 at 73.

q: Where does the "fresh" scratch sound come from?
a: From the end of the B-side of "Change the Beat", a 1982 Celluloid Records 12-inch by Fab 5 Freddy and Beside. GrandMixer D.ST first scratched it on Herbie Hancock's "Rockit" in 1983.

q: What did Daft Punk sample for "One More Time"?
a: Eddie Johns's "More Spell on You" (1979, or 1978 in some listings). As of May 2021 Johns had received nothing; Daft Punk's representative said royalties are paid to the track's owner.

q: What keyboard preset is the Sleng Teng riddim?
a: The "rock" rhythm preset of the Casio Casiotone MT-40, a 1981 keyboard. The preset was written by Casio employee Okuda Hiroko, and Casio asks for a credit line and no fee.

q: Did The Verve get "Bitter Sweet Symphony" back from the Rolling Stones?
a: Yes. On May 23, 2019, Richard Ashcroft announced that Mick Jagger and Keith Richards had agreed that April to hand over their share and drop their writing credit.
